item.title: Google Gemini for macOS adds computer use for multi-step tasks
item.description:
Google Gemini for macOS adds computer use for multi-step tasks

Google’s Gemini app for macOS now includes a computer use feature that enables the AI assistant to perform multi-step tasks across local files, desktop applications, and the web.

🔍 Overview

  • Gemini can now help users “get multi-step tasks done across your local files, desktop apps, and the web”
  • Google suggests the feature is useful for speeding up workflows, filling in forms, making presentations, and listing items for sale
  • The company says Gemini can better help with filling in forms and creative workflows with this new capability

🧩 How it works

  • Users decide which apps Gemini can access
  • A background window shows a live preview in the chat so users can follow along as Gemini works

⚙️ Key details

  • Computer use enables interaction with local files, desktop apps, and web content
  • Supported use cases include form filling, presentation creation, sales listings, and general workflow acceleration
  • The feature operates within user-granted app permissions

🚀 Availability

  • Rolling out now in English for users in the US
  • Settings preview appeared with this week’s macOS 27.3 beta

💡 Why it matters

  • Google is introducing computer use ahead of Apple launching new restrictions for apps requesting “full disk access” on Mac
  • Apple’s planned restrictions cite potential risks from AI agents with computer use capabilities

#Google #Gemini #macOS #AIagents #computeruse

Source: Gemini on Mac can now use your computer

item.title: LCU Decouples Codex Computer Use for Any Agent Harness
item.description:
LCU Decouples Codex Computer Use for Any Agent Harness

A new tool called LCU (Local Computer Use) has emerged, decoupling Codex’s original computer-use runtime from the Codex app to make it usable inside any agent harness, without requiring Codex authentication.

🔍 Overview

LCU exposes the original Codex computer-use runtime to local harnesses. To function, the official ChatGPT desktop app must remain installed locally; it supplies the runtime and instructions, while LCU handles setup and integration.

🧩 How it works

  • Desktop Apps: The system can read windows, click, type, and take screenshots.
  • Browsers: When enabled, it can read and control Chrome tabs through the official extension, subject to site approval.
  • Approvals: The first time an agent controls an app, the computer-use runtime asks the user to allow it.
  • Security: Only the user can answer the approval pane; the model cannot see, press, or fake the pane.

⚙️ Key details

  • Harness Adapters: Adapters are available for Pi, Codex CLI, and Claude Code, with experimental integrations for Oh My Pi, Hermes, DeepSeek Harness, and Junie.
  • Junie Limitations: With Junie, the agent cannot show LCU’s per-app prompt. Instead, it runs lcu apps allow <App> itself, and approval lasts permanently until the user revokes it.
  • High-Risk Apps: Browsers and password managers display warnings from the runtime. Apps that Computer Use outright refuses, such as Terminal and iTerm2, are declined. The app hosting the agent is never approved.
  • CLI Management: Users can review and change the approved app list from the terminal on macOS without opening the Codex app. Listing apps is free, but allowing or revoking requires the user to be at the machine.
Integration Details
Claude Code Requires version 2.1.287 or newer.
Claude App Register LCU through Claude Code (lcu setup --agent claude-code), not through Settings > Connectors.
Claude Code Mod The lcu-approve mod asks approval questions natively as a card in the app and an approval pane in the terminal.
Turn Limits In Claude Code, Computer Use normally ends when the turn that started it ends. A background subagent will be told “Computer Use is unavailable” unless an opt-in setting keeps it available for every turn of the session.

🚀 Availability

  • Mac Requirements: Requires an Apple Silicon Mac for Claude Code integration.
  • Setup: Setup involves two commands through the Claude Code plugin manager.
  • Command: Use /computer-use-apps to open an Approved apps panel in the terminal, displaying always-allowed apps with a Revoke option and an Allow field.

#LCU #ComputerUse #AIagents #Claude #DeveloperTools

Source: amontlabs/lcu

item.title: open-computer-use expands platform support and adds macOS Locked Use
item.description:
open-computer-use expands platform support and adds macOS Locked Use

open-computer-use, an open‑source Computer Use service wrapped as MCP, has expanded its platform support and added a macOS locked‑use feature.

🔍 Overview

  • open-computer-use is an open‑source Computer Use service wrapped as MCP.
  • Inspired by OpenAI’s Codex Computer Use.
  • Built on Accessibility to create non‑intrusive CUA.

🧩 How It Works

  • Any AI agent or MCP client can run Computer Use on macOS, Linux, and Windows.
  • Gemini CLI connects through MCP to run full Computer Use actions.
  • In Codex App and Codex CLI, it matches official experience.

⚙️ Key Details

Installation

  • Install the skill directly.
  • Install for Codex.
  • Install for Claude Code.
  • Update an existing global install, including Codex install created above.
  • Manually download and install the open‑computer‑use skill.

Usage

  • Call a single Computer Use tool and print the MCP‑style JSON result.
  • Run a sequence in one process to reuse element_index state.
  • Sequence sleeps 1s between successful operations by default.

Permissions

  • On macOS, run once and grant Accessibility and Screen Recording.
  • Windows and Linux do not require this step.
  • Check permissions; onboarding opens only when missing.
  • macOS: query permission JSON without opening onboarding.

Configuration

  • ocu supports global configuration starting with version 1.0.0.
  • Default configuration file: ~/.config/ocu/config.json.

Locked Use (macOS)

  • Locked Use is now supported on macOS.
  • OCU temporarily unlocks the Mac after it has been locked so the agent can continue working.
  • Protective services such as a full‑screen shield are in place during use.
  • See the Locked Use guide for setup, installed components, and permissions.

Runtime Requirements (macOS)

Requirement Detail
macOS version 14.0 or later
Permissions Accessibility & Screen Recording
Steps Run once to grant permissions

🚀 Availability

  • Running on Linux.
  • macOS runtime requires macOS 14.0+.
  • Windows and Linux require no special permissions.

💡 Why it Matters

  • Has become one of the most useful workflows for nearly 100 % AI‑generated projects.
  • Built on open source, enabling quick setup with the harness template.
  • Offers a non‑intrusive, accessibility‑based solution for Computer Use across major OSes.

For more on the methodology behind this project, see the post at https://www.ifuryst.com/blog/2026/speedrunning-the-ai-era/

#OpenAI #ComputerUse #AIAgents #macOS #Accessibility

Source: iFurySt/open-computer-use

item.title: OpenAI launches GPT‑6.1 Terra focused on visual reasoning and computer use
item.description:
OpenAI launches GPT‑6.1 Terra focused on visual reasoning and computer use

On 26 October 2026 OpenAI announced GPT‑6.1 Terra, a fast, efficient model that combines detailed visual reasoning and precise computer use with clearer, more natural writing.

🔍 Overview

  • Positioned between the cheapest and most expensive offerings, similar to Anthropic’s Sonnet model.
  • Marketed as a step up from GPT‑5.6 Terra.
  • Targets work‑day tasks such as drafting proposals, interpreting technical drawings, filling out forms, and editing videos.

🧩 Capabilities

  • Visual reasoning – detailed analysis of images and technical drawings.
  • Computer use – automation of repetitive, computer‑based tasks.
  • Technical communication – clearer, more natural writing for proposals and documentation.

⚙️ Key Details

  • Pricing: $1 per million input tokens and $5 per million output tokens.
  • This pricing is almost half that of GPT‑5.6 Terra and GPT‑6.1 Sol, and about 10 times the price of GPT‑6 Luna.
  • Model positioning (per OpenAI’s Ted Sanders on Hacker News):
    • Better than Astra and Sol at technical communication.
    • Similar vision and computer‑use ability to Astra and Sol, but much faster.
    • Slightly weaker than those models on most other tasks.
  • Cost‑performance trade‑off:
    • For API developers, Terra is a mid‑range option: cheaper than Sol yet smarter than Luna, especially for vision, computer use, and communication.
    • For subscribers, Terra can extend usage limits and provide clearer communication and faster computer use without being a “bombshell” release.

🚀 Availability

  • Offered through OpenAI’s API for developers.
  • Available to ChatGPT Plus subscribers as a selectable model option.
  • Intended for tasks that benefit from a balance of cost and capability, such as automated form filling or video editing workflows.

📊 Comparison with Other Frontier Models

Model Relative Cost (vs Terra) Highlighted Strengths (vs Terra)
GPT‑6.1 Terra Baseline ( $1 /M in, $5 /M out ) Fast visual reasoning, precise computer use, clear writing
GPT‑6.1 Sol Roughly 2× Terra’s price Comparable vision/computer use, slower
GPT‑6 Astra Similar price tier Terra better at technical communication
GPT‑6 Luna ≈ 10× cheaper than Terra Terra smarter for vision, computer use, communication

Cost and performance remarks reflect the statements made by OpenAI and community comments on the announcement.

#OpenAI #GPT-6.1 #AIModels #VisualReasoning #ComputerUse

Source: GPT-6.1 Terra

item.title: OpenAI Releases GPT-6 Astra with Advanced Computer Use and Graphical Capabilities
item.description:
OpenAI Releases GPT-6 Astra with Advanced Computer Use and Graphical Capabilities

OpenAI has released GPT-6 Astra, a new model that significantly improves upon its predecessor, GPT-5.6, across multiple categories. While the model shows progress in writing, math, and coding, it is particularly distinguished by its graphical capabilities and its ability to interact with local computer interfaces.

🔍 Overview

GPT-6 Astra represents a major step forward, outperforming the previous GPT-5.6 model in nearly all evaluated areas. It is particularly noted for:

  • Leapfrogging GPT-5.6 in math, coding, and writing.
  • Exceptional performance in image and rendering tasks.
  • The ability to operate local software through the Codex/ChatGPT app.

⚙️ Key details

Independent evaluations from Artificial Analysis provide a look at the model’s performance relative to existing benchmarks. GPT-6 Astra achieved a 99.9% score on the ARC-AGI-3 benchmark, which measures logic puzzles and generalization, while its predecessor GPT-5.6 Sol reached 7.8%.

Benchmark or Index Details
ARC-AGI-3 Measures logic puzzles and generalization; Astra achieved 99.9%.
Coding Agent Index v1.4 A blend of agentic coding tasks where Astra is currently at the frontier.
Intelligence Index v4.2 A general index blending various task types, including Terminal-Bench v2.1.
Computer Use A capability where the model interacts with GUIs via the mouse cursor on local machines.

🧩 How it works

Evaluation accuracy depends on the specific harness used during testing. While models are often optimized for a primary harness during training, independent benchmarks use various setups to provide more trustworthy results:

  • Stirrup: An open-source, minimal harness used by GDPval-AA and AA-Briefcase.
  • Terminus 2: The harness used for Terminal-Bench v2.1 within the Intelligence Index.
  • τ-Bench: The harness utilized for τ³-Banking evaluations.

💡 Why it matters

The model’s computer use capability allows it to operate software on a local machine, which is demonstrated through intuitive graphical tasks. Notable examples of this performance include:

  • Modeling and rendering a 3D version of New York City in Blender.
  • Conducting virtual open house tours.
  • Using the mouse cursor to interact with a browser version of MS Paint to redraw images (demonstrated using Astra Medium and High variants).

While traditional LLM strengths include text-based tasks like writing and API usage, Astra’s ability to navigate graphical user interfaces represents a maturing frontier in model capabilities.

#OpenAI #GPT6 #Astra #AIagents #ComputerUse

Source: GPT-6 Astra, Looped Transformers, and Hidden Reasoning
